architecture_decisions: The proposed architecture decision is to implement a deterministic first-agent rejection followed by alternate assignment, finite alternate exhaustion, fresh dispatch identities and no new model loop.
work_items: The proposed work item is to implement a deterministic first-agent rejection followed by alternate assignment, finite alternate exhaustion, fresh dispatch identities and no new model loop.
validations: The proposed validation is to implement a deterministic first-agent rejection followed by alternate assignment, finite alternate exhaustion, fresh dispatch identities and no new model loop.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — A first assigned hosted implementation agent whose proposal is rejected by the protected proposal validator does not immediately terminate IMPLEMENT when another admitted eligible agent exists.
AC-02: validate protected requirement — The alternate attempt uses a different eligible agent identity, incremented assignment generation, and fresh operation/request/attempt identity.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — The rejected proposal causes no canonical workspace mutation, lineage acceptance, Git mutation, deployment, REVIEW completion, or Engineering Run transition.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — A successful alternate proposal continues through the existing exact acceptance-coverage checks and ordinary disposable candidate validation, independent evaluation, routing and competition path.
AC-05: validate protected requirement — Recovery attempts are deterministic and bounded by `max_reassignments_per_work_unit`; no unbounded model loop is possible.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — If every eligible alternate fails generation/validation, IMPLEMENT fails closed with bounded `candidate_generation_failure` evidence whose reason is `CANDIDATE_GENERATION_EXHAUSTED`, with `worker_process_loss=false` and no raw provider/model output or secrets.
AC-07: validate protected requirement — Existing process-loss and lease-expiry worker reassignment semantics remain unchanged.
AC-08: validate protected requirement — Existing successful single-agent and multi-agent paths remain unchanged when the first assigned agent succeeds.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Tests prove deterministic first-agent rejection followed by alternate assignment, finite alternate exhaustion, fresh dispatch identities and no new authority claims.
AC-10: validate protected requirement — Protected spec/plan validation, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, client/browser, protected promotion and DSPy release gates are green before merge.
